events.label: Revolt against Emperor Henry IV
events.labelCn: 起兵反对皇帝亨利四世
events.note: Forced his father to abdicate on 31 December 1105.

events.label: King of Germany
events.labelCn: 成为德意志国王
events.note: Anointed and crowned on 5-6 January 1106 after his father's forced abdication; he had first been crowned co-ruler at Aachen on 6 January 1099.

events.label: Seizure of Pope Paschal II
events.labelCn: 拘押教皇帕斯卡尔二世
events.note: The pope was captured in February 1111 after the cancelled coronation of 12 February; the Treaty of Ponte Mammolo followed on 12 April 1111.

events.label: Imperial coronation
events.labelCn: 加冕为神圣罗马帝国皇帝

events.label: Marriage to Matilda of England
events.labelCn: 与英格兰的玛蒂尔达成婚
events.note: Wedding celebrations in Mainz; the engagement had been made at Utrecht at Easter 1110.

events.label: Concordat of Worms
events.labelCn: 《沃尔姆斯宗教协定》
events.note: Ended the Investiture Controversy between emperor and papacy.

events.label: Death at Utrecht
events.labelCn: 在乌得勒支去世
events.note: Died of disease; modern accounts often attribute it to cancer. He was the last Salian emperor; the marriage produced no surviving legitimate heirs.

deathCause.summary: Died of disease at Utrecht (commonly attributed to cancer)
deathCause.detail: Henry V died on 23 May 1125 at Utrecht. Contemporary sources record death from disease; later accounts commonly attribute it to cancer. His body was buried at Speyer. As the last Salian emperor he left no surviving legitimate heirs, and the crown passed to Lothair of Supplinburg.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在乌得勒支因病去世（常归因于癌症）
deathCause.detailCn: 1125 年 5 月 23 日，亨利五世在乌得勒支去世。时人记载为疾病所致，后世常归因于癌症。其遗体葬于施派尔。作为萨利安王朝最后一位皇帝，他没有留下存活的合法继承人，王位转由洛泰尔三世继承。

sourceNote: First husband of Empress Matilda; marriage ended after his death.
notes: Holy Roman Emperor and first husband of Empress Matilda. Birth date uncertain: probably 11 August 1081 or 1086 (sources disagree). German spelling 'Heinrich' is preserved per project convention.

notes: Holy Roman Emperor remembered for the Investiture Controversy and his penance at Canossa; deposed by his son Heinrich V.

deathCause.detail: Deposed by his son Heinrich V, Heinrich IV died at Liège on 7 August 1106; his death is recorded as from illness.

fullNameCn: 施派尔的亨利（沃尔姆斯的亨利）

events.label: Fathered the future emperor Conrad II
events.labelCn: 成为后来皇帝康拉德二世之父
events.note: Conrad II was born around 990 into the Salian family; Henry's own death is variously dated to 990/991, 989–992, or in older tradition 997.

sourceNote: Deutsche Biographie, 'Heinrich von Worms/Heinrich von Speyer'; Herwig Wolfram, Conrad II, 990–1039; Peter H. Wilson, Heart of Europe; Wikipedia used only as a supplementary cross-check.
notes:
A short-lived Salian nobleman whose principal dynastic importance is as the father of Emperor Conrad II. He died before the Salian rise to kingship and never held a royal title.

Confidence / caveats: His chronology is unusually uncertain: modern reference works give death in 990 or 991, while other traditions broaden it to 989–992 or place it as late as 997. Birth c.970 is approximate. His mother's identity and his precise comital jurisdiction are not uniformly presented in the sources; 'Count in the Wormsgau' is safer than assigning a later territorial title. Because his independent career is poorly documented, he is rated below 5 rather than padding the timeline with conjectural events.

events.label: Betrothed to Frederick of Staufen as he received the Duchy of Swabia
events.labelCn: 在腓特烈获授士瓦本公国之际与其订婚
events.note: The betrothal tied Emperor Henry IV's Salian dynasty directly to Frederick of Staufen as he received the Duchy of Swabia.

events.label: Married Frederick I, Duke of Swabia
events.labelCn: 与士瓦本公爵腓特烈一世结婚
events.note: The marriage joined the Salian princess Agnes to the rising Hohenstaufen ducal house in Swabia.

events.label: Was widowed by Frederick I's death
events.labelCn: 腓特烈一世去世后守寡
events.note: After Frederick I's death, their sons Frederick II and Conrad III carried the Salian bloodline into the Hohenstaufen dynasty.

events.label: Married Leopold III, Margrave of Austria
events.labelCn: 与奥地利边区侯利奥波德三世结婚
events.note: The second marriage linked the Salian imperial family to Leopold III and the Babenberg dynasty in Austria.

events.label: Died at Klosterneuburg
events.labelCn: 在克洛斯特新堡去世
events.note: Agnes died at Klosterneuburg after decades as a dynastic link between the Salian, Hohenstaufen and Babenberg houses.

sourceNote: Deutsche Biographie, 'Agnes von Waiblingen'; Peter Csendes and Austrian Babenberg scholarship; Karl Lechner, Die Babenberger; Wolfgang Muschka, Agnes von Waiblingen; Wikipedia only for cross-checking exact dates.
notes:
Agnes is the crucial female bridge from the Salian emperors to the Hohenstaufen kings: her son Conrad III became the first Hohenstaufen king of Germany, while Frederick II of Swabia fathered Barbarossa. Her second marriage also connected the Salian inheritance to the Babenbergs.

Confidence / caveats: Her birth date is disputed: modern works variously give 1072/73 or 1074/75, so birthYear is left null rather than selecting a false precision. Medieval sources attribute a very large number of children to her second marriage, and exact child lists vary; the family list includes the principal securely identifiable offspring rather than attempting every disputed child.
